text:
Dead of Ninety-two and Ninety-three,

who, pale from the kiss freedom gives,

calmly shattered with your clogs the yoke

that weighs upon the soul and brow of the world;


Ecstatic men, great in the storm,

you whose love leapt wrapped in rags,

soldiers whom Death, noble Lover, sowed

through the ancient furrows to regenerate them;


whose blood washed sullied grandeur clean.

Dead there at Valmy, at Fleurus, in Italy,

million Christs, Dead, with gentle, dark eyes;


sleep with the Republic, while we go

bent beneath kings as beneath a lash.

—For it is the Cassagnacs who remember you now.

translation.title: Dead of Ninety-Two and Ninety-Three
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Rimbaud's revolutionary apostrophe and the bitter final turn toward reactionary commemoration.
